reason: At base REGEX_FORMAT is Y{1,4} and format() only implements YY/YYYY, so unmatched 'Y' and 'YYY' fall through to the zoneStr/timezone-offset fallback instead of returning literal text, so the expected 'Y' and '24Y'-style outputs would not be produced.

After the fix REGEX_FORMAT only matches YYYY|YY, so a lone 'Y' isn't matched by replace() and stays literal, and 'YYY' matches 'YY' leaving the trailing 'Y' literal, exactly matching the expected outputs.

This PR is a pure refactor extracting the existing 'contains %, then decode' logic into tryDecodeURIComponent; the same decoding behavior (param.indexOf('%') check then decodeURIComponent) already existed inline at base, so percent-encoded route params were already decoded correctly.
The refactor preserves identical decode semantics (tryDecodeURIComponent still checks for '%' then decodes), so percent-encoded params continue to decode correctly after the change.

The PR description explicitly states this regression test 'fails before the change and passes after' -- at base, reschedule() updates Redis via zincrby but never updates @score, so entry.score/entry.at on the same in-memory handle stay stale.
After the fix, reschedule() sets @score = at.to_f, so the in-memory entry immediately reflects the new time, matching the test's expectation.

This test only exercises Content-Type/charset parsing, a feature completely untouched by the Range-header whitespace-trimming PR; ktor's ContentType parsing already correctly extracts type/subtype/charset before this change.
Same unrelated Content-Type parsing behavior; the Range header diff does not affect ContentType parsing, so this continues to pass after the change.

The PR only changes error-message sanitization in ComposerRepository and does not touch archive/zip timestamp handling, so whatever the pre-existing (unrelated) archive-timestamp behavior is, it is unaffected by this diff; assuming normal Composer archiving preserves mtimes as intended.
Same reasoning as the base case: this PR does not touch the ZipArchiver/archive timestamp code path at all, so behavior should be identical to base for this unrelated test.

This test exercises System.Text.Json async deserialization with a nullable parent property, a feature entirely unrelated to the CredentialCache path-comparison PR; assuming no other described defect, this should behave normally.
Same JSON deserialization scenario, unaffected by the unrelated CredentialCache diff; sync and async deserialization of the same payload should already be equivalent.
INET <<= ANY subquery support is a standard, pre-existing CockroachDB SQL feature unrelated to the FETCH FIRST/WITH HOLD cursor fix in this diff, so it should parse and execute normally at base.
INET >>= ANY over an array is likewise unrelated to the cursor FETCH FIRST fix; no evidence this diff touches INET operators or ANY-array comparisons.

At base, get_environment_proxies() always prefixes NO_PROXY entries with a wildcard ('all://*::1'), which is an invalid/unparseable URL pattern for an IPv6 address, so client construction with NO_PROXY='::1' would raise rather than succeed -- exactly the bug this PR fixes.
After the fix, IPv6 hostnames are detected and wrapped as 'all://[::1]', a valid pattern, so client construction with NO_PROXY='::1' succeeds as expected.

This is precisely the regression described: at base, Series.str.match with flags=re.DOTALL (any flag other than IGNORECASE) raises because of the overly strict flag-equality check, so the DOTALL-enabled match against 'a\nc' would error rather than return the expected boolean results.

The PR restores support for non-IGNORECASE flags like DOTALL both via flags= and via a precompiled pattern, matching the test's exact scenario (new test_match_non_ignorecase_flags_applied covers this).

The bug fixed here is about broken recursive result-parent tracking when a group sits in the middle of a chain followed by more elements; a chain of task->group->group->task closely matches that failure pattern, so serializing/reconstructing the AsyncResult tree would likely lose child results for one of the groups before the fix.
After the fix, prev_task/prev_res are correctly updated after each chain step, so the parent-result chain (and thus tuple serialization/deserialization) should preserve all four group children.

The PR specifically fixes value_terminator only when '--' is the very first argument (empty first positional); the benchmark scenario has two values already collected before '--', which is a different, previously-working code path (an existing similar test, value_terminator_restores_escaping_disabled_by_allow_hyphen_values, already covers a non-first-arg terminator case), so this likely already passed at base.

This scenario continues to work after the fix as well, since the change only adds handling for the previously-broken first-argument case without altering the already-working non-first-argument terminator behavior.

This PR only reorders when @derive is read at compile time to reduce unnecessary compile-time module dependencies for Inspect derivation; it has no effect on changeset validation/required-field logic, so required-field validation continues to work normally at base.

Same reasoning as base: this is a compile-time-dependency-only change with no runtime behavior effect on Ecto.Changeset validation, so required-field validation still works correctly after the change.

At base, the OSC11 background handler calls nvim_set_option_value without noautocmd, so once startup has finished (starting=false) a background color change fires OptionSet normally, and background changes also trigger a ColorScheme reload as standard Vim/Neovim behavior. Nothing in base suppresses these for a post-startup change.

The fix wraps the OSC11-driven background set in vim.cmd("noautocmd set background=..."), which unconditionally blocks all autocommand events (both OptionSet and ColorScheme) for every invocation of this handler, not just the startup race case. Since the diff shows no conditional gating on startup vs. later changes, a genuine post-startup terminal color change would also have OptionSet/ColorScheme suppressed at head, so the test expecting both to fire would fail.
